key_insight: A generalized swimming formula describes microswimmers in fluids with anisotropic and odd viscosity, where the scallop theorem still holds but orientational dynamics can change.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide microswimmer control and transport design in chiral or anisotropic viscous media.
method: Apply the generalized Lorentz reciprocal theorem to establish Onsager–Casimir reciprocity for rigid-body resistance tensors.
Relate swimming velocities linearly to prescribed surface motion and imposed background flows.
Analyze a spherical swimmer in an odd-viscous fluid under shear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical derivations showing that sufficiently strong shear destabilizes bimodal chirotactic alignment, without describing experimental or numerical validation.
watch_item: Applicability is restricted to low-Reynolds-number, linearly viscous fluids; nonlinear rheology lies outside the stated framework.
paper_title: Swimming formula in a linearly viscous fluid with anisotropic and odd viscosity tensors at low Reynolds number
